    Common Attributes
    Build out as many common features as this project needs — a window balance, a mini-fridge cabinet, an in-room safe, and so on — each with its own coverage: one might go on every room type, the next on most of them, another on just a handful. Define each one once, apply it to whichever Room Types need it, and each applied copy stays independently editable afterward.
    Apply “Attribute” to Room Types
    Check the Room Types below, then click Apply. Unchecked, untouched types get a fresh copy at the values below. Room Types that already have this applied are tagged Applied and start unchecked too — check one back in to push a global correction (name, qty, rate, reference) to its existing copy; leave it unchecked to leave that room exactly as it is.
    ⚠ Checking a Room Type already tagged Applied will overwrite its existing item's name, qty, rate, and reference with what's above — not just newly-checked ones. Leave it unchecked to leave that room untouched.
    Rename Everywhere
    This pushes a new elevation/group name out to 0 room types that already have “Attribute” applied — on demand, only when you click Rename, never automatically. If a room type's bucket also holds other applied items, they'll show under the new name too since they share the same elevation.

    Per-Box Calculator — DS Perimeter FormulaPerim = W+W+D+H • Min 50 li • +$1.35 handling/box

    DS Formula: Price/box = (Perim × Li Rate) + Per Box Base + $1.35 handling. Example: 18"W × 4"H × 21"D → Perim 61 li × $0.46 = $28.06 + $35.88 + $1.35 = $65.29/box

    Material & Finish Schedule — By Area ▼
    Assign material tags (PT-1, PL-1, etc.) matching the architectural finish schedule. Each tag defines the material/finish for that area — like an architect's finish plan.
    Examples: PT-1 = Sherwin-Williams Repose Gray SW-7015, Satin • PL-1 = Formica 7732-58 Calacatta Marble, Matte • ST-1 = Maple Natural Stain, Satin CV
    Wood Species & Cut ▼
    One row per species / application. Solid stock is SAWN, veneer is SLICED — the cut list changes with the form, because "plain sawn veneer" is not a thing and specifying it that way is how a job gets rejected at submittal. Add as many species as the job carries; standing & running trim, doors and casework can each be different.
    Examples: White Oak, Solid, Rift Sawn — standing & running trim • White Oak, Veneer, Rift Cut, Book Match — panels • Hard Maple, Solid, Plain Sawn — paint-grade face frames
    Exposed Surface Finish Schedule ▼
    For laminate / HPL exposed surfaces. Group by surface (Countertops, Cabinets, etc.) and list every approved manufacturer/pattern as an equal alternate — e.g. Wilsonart #4656-60 "Bronze Legacy", Formica #7698-58 "Ashen Ceramic" Matte, Nevamar #MR2005T "Taupe Matrix" can all be listed under Countertops as acceptable options.
    ⚙ Hardware & Pull Schedule — By Area ▼
    Pulls and hardware can vary by area. Define each area's pull spec here — overrides the global hardware selection for that area.
    Example: Lobby — 5" bar pull, Matte Black • Break Room — 3-3/4" bin pull, Brushed Nickel

    ❓ Help & User Guide

    The full lifecycle of a job — estimate and win it, then engineer, purchase, build, schedule, ship, and bill it. New here? Load the training project (Database tab) so every screen is populated as you read, then start with Quick Start below. Every screen also has a hint bar at the top — it shows what's required before that page, and the ❓ Guide button opens a short training card with the workflow order. Tap any section header to expand it.

    Quick Start — a job front to back

    ▶
    The app is built around one path: Project → Areas → Elevations → Line Items. Fill it top-down and every other tab (finish, breakdown, proposal) populates itself.
    1

    Set up the project

    In the left sidebar, fill Project Info — job name, proposal #, client, date, address. Pick a Project Tier (Standard, Commercial, or Premium). The tier drives which rate column new line items pull from, so set it first.

    2

    Add areas, then elevations

    Click + Area for each room (Kitchen, Bath, Pantry…). Select an area, then add elevations inside it (North Wall, Island, Upper Perimeter). Elevations are how you organize line items and where you attach dimensions and an architect drawing reference via ✎ Dims.

    3

    Build the estimate line by line

    On the ✎ Estimate tab, add line items to each elevation. Pick a category (upper/lower cabinets, countertops, doors, hardware, trim…) — the unit, CSI spec section, and tier rate auto-fill. Enter quantity; the extended cost calculates instantly. Pull common items from your Item Library to save typing.

    4

    Layer in the specialty tabs

    Use Drawer Boxes for DS-618 perimeter pricing, Finish & Paint (auto-fills square footage from your cabinets), plus Mobilization and ⚖ Prev. Wage when a job calls for travel or Davis-Bacon compliance. Only what you enable rolls into the total.

    5

    Tune markups, then deliver the proposal

    In the sidebar totals, set Waste %, Contingency %, Markup % and Tax to land your client price. Go to Summary, use ⚡ Auto-Draft Scope, fill terms, then Print / PDF. Log the bid to your CRM with Log Bid.

    ✓ You never have to "save." Every change auto-saves to this browser instantly. To keep a portable copy in Google Drive, set a save location once (see Saving & Sync).

    How the estimate is built

    ▶
    Project → Area (room) → Elevation (wall / run) → Line Item (priced unit)  →  totals roll upward automatically.
    Area
    A room or zone — Kitchen, Master Bath, Mudroom. Carries a color tag and appears in the sidebar and cost breakdown.
    Elevation
    A wall or cabinet run within an area. Holds line items and can carry dimensions plus an architect drawing/detail reference.
    Line Item
    A single priced entry: category, unit, quantity, rate, and an auto-filled CSI MasterFormat spec section.
    Extended cost
    Quantity × tier rate for that line, summed up the chain.

    How the sidebar total is assembled

    • Materials & Labor — sum of every line item
    • + Contingency % — risk buffer (default 0)
    • + Waste % — material yield loss (default 5)
    • + Markup % — your margin (default 20)
    • = Client Price — optional Tax % on top

    Adjust any percentage in the sidebar and the client price recalculates live.

    Cost codes & splits: Every category maps to a CSI cost code (KI1000 Kitchen, BA1000 Bath, etc.). The Breakdown tab uses these to split each line across Labor / Material / Equipment / Sub / Overhead for a proper cost report.

    What every tab does

    ▶
    ✎ EstimateThe core. Build areas, elevations, and priced line items — or, on repetitive work, Room Types with an occurrence roster instead. Attach elevation dimensions and drawing references. See Room Types & Bulk Import below.
    Mass EditVerify Common Attributes across every Room Type they're applied to — mismatches, applied-line counts, and bulk apply/sync in one grid.
    Drawer BoxesSet the project drawer-box standard (DS 618 Maple Dovetail default) and price any box with the DS perimeter formula, then push it into the current elevation.
    Finish & PaintFinish cost by square foot — auto-estimated from your cabinet faces and flagged finished end panels. Cost-plus material + labor.
    + Change OrdersLog additions/deductions after contract. Approved COs roll into the project total; pending ones don't.
    SummaryScope narrative, inclusions/exclusions, terms & schedule, price summary, and the printable client proposal.
    ⚙ Pricing & LibraryThe cabinet pricing matrix (all three tiers), drawer/finish rates, and your reusable Item Library shared across projects.
    Bid LogCRM-style bid tracker with lead source — won/lost/pending history saved to MaxCraft_BidLog.json.
    Addenda & RFIsFormal correspondence log — addendum acknowledgment and architect RFI routing, with RFI-blast draft emails and letters of transmittal.
    BreakdownCost analysis grouped by category, area, or cost code — split into Labor / Material / Equipment / Sub / Overhead. The Alternates & VE sub-tab prices optional add/deduct/substitution items the client can accept before award, separate from the Base Contract Total.
    MobilizationTrips, mileage (IRS rate or actual fuel), travel labor, tolls, vehicle, and per diem. Toggle on to fold into the total.
    ⚖ Prev. WageDavis-Bacon / prevailing wage — craft classifications, fringe, OT multipliers, and a certified-payroll compliance checklist.
    CRMCompanies, contacts, introductions, and distribution lists that feed the RFI-blast and transmittal recipient pickers.
    Post-Award — unlocked when a project is awarded
    PlanningRolling this-week / next-week task board with department, assignee, hours, and production sync.
    EngineeringRelease to production, hardware/material schedules, plus Eng. Specs, Drafting Brief, and the Installation plan.
    PurchasingBudget vs. actual, vendor catalog, purchase orders, and receiving with 3-way match.
    Work OrdersShop travelers auto-generated from the Bill of Operations, with per-operation checkoffs.
    SubmittalsTransmittal log with AWI statuses and an integrated sample tracker.
    ProductionMulti-project overview, materials due-in, the draggable Gantt, and the operations list.
    Cut ListParametric cabinet parts, the cut bill, a CutRite-style panel optimizer, and a purchasing material list.
    Pack-OutThe field tool & equipment checklist with van/shop/site tagging.
    WarrantyCloseout checklist and warranty register; prints a closeout binder.
    LogisticsReleases, truck lots, QR labels, the phone scanner, and progress billing.
    Always available
    Spec ReviewThe full construction spec with chip pickers, Material & Build libraries, templates, and the Build Report.
    DatabaseTraining project, automation settings, PostgreSQL utility, and file locations.
    BinderAssembles the full physical-binder package — cover, contents, tab dividers, and every document.

    Room Types, Common Attributes & bulk room import

    ▶

    For repetitive work — a hotel, student housing, a multifamily building — you don't draw two hundred identical rooms one at a time. You price a handful of Room Types once and attach an occurrence roster naming every physical room of that type. Change the Room Type and every room on its roster changes with it.

    Room Type
    A reusable cabinetry template — build its elevations and line items once, exactly like a normal Area. Click + Type in the sidebar Room Types panel.
    Occurrence roster
    The list of physical rooms priced by that type. Open Manage Roster to add rows manually or via CSV.
    Needs Pricing
    A Room Type with no elevations yet carries this badge so an empty one can't quietly ship in a proposal.

    Common Attributes

    Click ⚙ Attributes to define something once — a specific pull, a countertop allowance, an install charge — and stamp it into any number of Room Types via an opt-in checklist. Each stamped copy becomes an independent line item; editing the attribute definition afterward does not silently rewrite rooms that already have it — you re-open Apply… and deliberately push the correction. Deleting an attribute is the one action that strips it everywhere automatically. Use the Mass Edit tab to audit coverage and mismatches across every Room Type at once.

    Importing a room list from CSV

    Two entry points: ↑ Import CSV in the Areas toolbar imports a whole property at once; Manage Roster → Import CSV on a single Room Type imports room numbers into just that one type. Paste or upload a list with a Room Type column and the importer does the sorting for you:

    • Suggested Grouping. After you map columns, a panel tallies how many times each Room Type name repeats. Names that repeat (or match a Room Type that already exists in the project) default to a grouped Room Type with a roster; names that show up only once become their own single Area instead of a padded one-room Room Type. Un-check or re-check any group before importing to override the suggestion either way.
    • Full-list guard on the single-type importer. If you paste a whole property's room list into a single Room Type's roster importer, the app detects the multiple distinct Room Type names and warns you before every row gets assigned to that one type — with a one-click button to switch to the full grouping-aware importer instead.
    Sample data note. The single-Room-Type "Import Roster" screen has no Room Type column of its own — every row you paste there is assigned to the one type you opened it from. If your list covers more than one room type, use the general ↑ Import CSV button (or let the warning banner switch you over) so rooms land in the right place.

    Needs Scope

    Click ⚠ Needs Scope next to the Room Types panel to review every Room Type and Area that has zero elevations — nothing priced, no cabinetry built. Check any combination and either Apply to Selected… a Common Attribute in bulk (Room Types only) or Delete Selected to clean up ones you don't need. A large CSV import opens this review automatically since a big room list can create dozens of blank entries at once.

    Incremental re-imports are safe. A row whose Room Type name matches one that already exists in the project always routes into that Room Type's roster — regardless of how many times it appears in this particular file — so you can top up a roster with a follow-up import without creating duplicates.

    After you win: the post-award workflow

    ▶

    Estimating is only half the app. The moment a job is awarded, a whole production & delivery system unlocks.

    Marking a project awarded. Open the project, and in the sidebar Project Info panel tick Project Awarded (or flip it in the Bid Log). That reveals a second group of tabs in the left rail: Planning, Engineering, Purchasing, Work Orders, Submittals, Production, Pack-Out, Warranty, and Logistics. Turn on Preview mode in the Database tab to see these tabs on any project while you learn.

    The natural order of a job.

    1 · Engineering
    Release the job to production: cut-list & CNC notes, hardware/material schedules (auto-pull from the estimate), and the release pipeline. Also holds the Eng. Specs, Drafting Brief, and Installation plan.
    2 · Purchasing
    Budget vs. actual, vendor catalog, purchase orders, and receiving (3-way match). Committed cost moves to spent as POs are received.
    3 · Work Orders
    Shop travelers generated from the Bill of Operations (boxes/doors/drawers/finishing × quantity), with per-operation checkboxes.
    4 · Submittals
    Transmittal log (AWI statuses) plus the sample tracker.
    5 · Production
    The detailed schedule — multi-project overview, materials due-in, and the draggable Gantt (see its own section below).
    6 · Pack-Out
    The 37-item field tool & equipment checklist with van/shop/site tagging.
    7 · Logistics
    Releases, truck lots, QR labels, the mobile scanner, and progress billing (its own section below).
    8 · Warranty
    Closeout checklist and warranty register; prints a closeout binder.
    ⚡ Let it build itself. With Automation on (Database tab), marking a job awarded auto-generates the production schedule and work orders. Every step still has manual buttons if you'd rather drive it yourself.

    Specialty buyouts & the purchase requisition. The Engineering and Spec Review tabs both have a Specialty Buyouts register for project-specific items (pull-outs, LED, custom pulls) — each with a description, a web hyperlink, vendor, quantity, and unit cost that rolls up as cost-of-goods toward the budget. Purchasing then has a Requisition tab that pulls everything the project needs — feedstock, hardware, and specialty — and groups it by vendor so you can issue one single-time-buy PO per vendor with a click.

    Putting a project on hold & notifying the team

    ▶

    When a job stalls — waiting on a client decision, a site issue, a payment holdup — flag it so it's visible everywhere the team looks, and send a quick heads-up without leaving the app.

    Marking it
    Tick Project On Hold in the sidebar (below the award section). A reason box appears — a short note on why and what's being waited on. Untick it to take the project off hold; the hold date clears automatically.
    Where it shows up
    A red ⚠ ON HOLD badge appears on the project's Workflow board header, the home page status strip, and in GM Command's cross-project banner (with your reason shown inline) so it can't be missed on a multi-project scan.
    Notify Team
    Click ✉ Notify Team (in the sidebar or right on the workflow banner) to open a short form — pick a recipient from your estimator/team list (or type another address), review the pre-filled subject and message, then Open Gmail Draft.
    Draft-only, same as everywhere else in this app. Notify Team opens a pre-filled Gmail compose window — nothing sends automatically. Review it in Gmail and hit Send yourself. The app has no SMS or chat integration; every "notify" feature works this same way.

    Weekly planning (this week / next week)

    ▶

    The Planning tab is a rolling two-week command center. It figures out the current week automatically and gives you three buckets: This Week, Next Week, and a Backlog.

    Add tasks to any bucket with department, assignee, estimated hours, and due date. Move them between weeks with the buttons on each card, set status (To Do / In Progress / Blocked / Done), and print the plan. Sync Production pulls any scheduled production operations that fall in the two-week window straight onto the board.

    Production schedule & the Gantt

    ▶

    The Production tab has four sub-tabs: All Projects, Materials Due In, Gantt Schedule, and Operations.

    All Projects shows every awarded job with its schedule span, a progress bar, next milestone, and a materials status chip. Materials Due In aggregates open PO lines across all active projects, sorted by expected arrival (order date + vendor lead time) — red is overdue, amber is due within 7 days.

    The Gantt. Click Generate Standard Schedule and the whole millwork template stands up in one click: six phases (Engineering → Procurement → Fabrication → Finishing → QC → Delivery) with 20 child operations, sequenced across workdays.

    Drag a bar
    Moves that task. A floating tooltip shows the new dates.
    Drag a phase
    Moves the whole phase — all its child tasks shift with it.
    Drag a task
    Its parent phase re-spans to still cover it. Parent/child stays intact.
    Right edge
    Resize a task's duration.
    Double-click
    Set a task's % complete; the phase rolls up automatically.
    Best on desktop or tablet. The bars are draggable with mouse or touch, but the day columns are narrow — a wide screen (Chrome/Edge) makes dragging comfortable.

    Cut list & panel optimizer

    ▶

    The Cut List tab is a parametric cabinet engine and a CutRite-style panel optimizer — a subset of Production & Work Orders that also feeds Purchasing.

    Build Method (your globals). The first sub-tab is the build method — the shop's construction standard that drives every cut size: frameless vs. face frame, face-frame material thickness (which reduces carcass depth and the side deduction), reveals, toe height, default top-drawer height, drawer joinery, and slide type. Undermount (Blum Tandem) and side mount each apply their own box-to-carcass clearance. Save a build method as a reusable template and load it into new projects so cabinets are built the same way every time.

    Parametric cabinets. Add a base, wall, or tall cabinet (or Pull from Estimate), then declare its face — doors, drawers, and layout. The engine computes openings, dividers, and drawer-box clearances for you (a face-frame two-door/two-drawer gets a center mullion and split openings), and re-cuts the numbers the moment you change a parameter:

    Back capture
    Groove, rabbet, plant-on, or nailer-only — each changes the back panel size (a grooved back grows by the groove depth on each side) and how the sides are machined.
    Base vs. wall/tall
    Base cabinets get a full bottom plus front/back cross rails; wall and tall get matching top & bottom panels.
    Shelves
    Fixed-shelf depth = carcass depth − nailer − back thickness. Adjustable-shelf depth is that minus a shelf setback (default 1/8").
    Drawer boxes
    Each drawer generates sides, front/back, and a bottom. Dovetail vs. doweled changes the front/back length; the bottom is sized from the groove. Drawer material is tracked separately from the carcass.

    Cut bill. The Cut Bill sub-tab lists every part — cabinet, part, material, thickness, quantity, length, width, and grain — and prints a shop-ready cut bill.

    Optimizer. Run the optimizer to nest all parts onto sheet stock with guillotine cuts, grouped by material and honoring grain direction (toggle enforcement on/off). You get sheet count, yield %, and a cut diagram per sheet — and a printable diagram set for the floor. Set sheet size, kerf, and cost per material on the Materials tab.

    Feeds Purchasing. The Materials tab rolls the nested sheets into a panel material requirement and Send to Purchasing drops a draft PO (sheets × cost per material) straight into the Purchasing module.

    Item Master & families. Cabinets come from the Item Master — a shared library of product styles grouped by family (base, drawer bank, sink, wall, tall, vanity). Each item can point at a build method, so a whole family shares one carcass construction. Click Item Master on the Cabinets tab, then Add to Job to drop a style into the current project; it carries that family's build method automatically.

    Component routing. Every generated part carries a routing — the operations it goes through before assembly (cut, edgeband which edges, CNC bore, dado, joinery). The Routing sub-tab lists each component with its edgeband edges and operation sequence, prints routing tickets / travelers for the floor, and totals the edgebanding linear-feet for purchasing.

    Materials — master to project to cabinet. Materials flow from an ERP Material Master (shared inventory of sheet stock, solid wood, edgeband, and hardware — hinges, slides, screws, shelf pins — each with cost, vendor, SKU, and on-hand count). The Project Materials sub-tab pulls what this job uses from the master and lets you add project-specific specialty buyouts (pull-outs, LED, custom pulls). Those project materials feed the build-method dropdowns, and specialty items can be assigned to the specific cabinets that require them. Hardware is auto-counted from the cabinets (hinges per door, slides per drawer, pins per adjustable shelf) and, together with the assigned specialty, rolls into a purchasing requirement you can send to Purchasing.

    Verify before cutting. The formulas assume frameless (Euro) construction with standard allowances. They're a strong starting point, but confirm your shop's specific allowances on the first run of any new part.

    Logistics: releases, truck lots & QR scanning

    ▶

    The Logistics tab turns finished cabinets into a tracked, scannable, billable delivery pipeline.

    Release
    Accounts for 100% of the product. "Generate Release from Estimate" creates one finished-good unit per cabinet (respecting quantities), each with a unique code and QR label.
    Unit lifecycle
    Pending → Produced → Staged (finished) → Loaded → Delivered. Advance units manually, in bulk, or by scanning.
    Truck lot
    A delivery. Build one, set the truck & driver, then load staged units onto it. One truck can carry units from multiple releases.
    Manifest
    Tracks exactly what units, from what release, are on which truck. Prints with signature lines and its own QR.
    Progress billing
    Value is recognized as goods advance (produced 40% / staged 60% / loaded 80% / delivered 100%), giving live % complete, earned-to-date, and delivered value against the contract.

    QR labels & the phone scanner. Print the label sheet and stick a QR on each finished good. Tap Scan to open the full-screen camera scanner on a phone. Pick a mode (Advance / Stage / Load / Deliver), point at a label, and the unit's status updates and logs with a timestamp. The header always shows % complete, % delivered, and how many finished goods remain — so a scan instantly tells you whether the job is done or there's still a balance. If a phone is turned, the preview auto-rotates; if the camera can't be used, type the code in manually.

    Scanner support. Live QR auto-detect uses the phone's built-in detector (Chrome on Android is best). On browsers without it, the camera still shows and manual entry always works.

    Spec Review, Material & Build Libraries

    ▶

    The Spec Review tab is the single source of truth for how a job is built — construction system, door style, box & drawer construction, hardware, finish, countertops, trim, and panels. Pick options with the chip buttons; use Templates to load a full commercial/residential preset in one click.

    Material Library
    Your custom materials — species, panel stock, hardware finishes. Added items become chip options everywhere.
    Build Library
    The non-material counterpart — custom construction methods, joinery, hardware mechanics, finish processes, trim profiles. Same idea: add once, use across all projects.

    Build Report. The Build Report button prints a professional, report-style PDF — the definitive "how we intend to build this project" spec document, with a cover, completeness bar, organized sections, and a sign-off block. It's the spec of record for the binder.

    New projects: intake & cabinet grade

    ▶

    Clicking + New opens a 3-step intake wizard: project details → cabinet grade → file location & confirm.

    Cabinet grade drives everything:

    Builder Grade
    Colors and sizes are limited to a supplier catalog, and the job is priced from a supplier quote (the "Bldr Quote" tab), not the custom cost engine. No AWI grade.
    Commercial / Semi-Custom / Premium Custom
    Opens the AWI quality grade choice and uses the full custom estimating engine.

    Design Intake Form. The Design Intake Form button (sidebar) opens a comprehensive, eight-section form for the design team — client info, cabinet grade, room scope, design specs, construction details, site conditions, budget/timeline, and notes. Fill it in-app (it saves to the project) or Print Blank to complete by hand in the field. Prints as a clean PDF with sign-off lines.

    The Project Binder

    ▶

    The Binder tab assembles a print-ready package for your physical binder: a cover, a table of contents, and a tab divider before every section, followed by the actual content of each document — project info, proposal, scope, change orders, engineering specs, drafting brief, submittals, POs, work orders, schedule, install plan, pack-out, warranty, and correspondence.

    Tick which sections to include, toggle the TOC and dividers, and hit Print Full Binder. Sections you file by hand (signed contract, approved shop drawings) print a labeled "physical insert" divider so the binder stays organized.

    Database, automation & the training project

    ▶

    The Database tab is mission control for the app itself.

    Training project
    Load test-project — a 100%-populated sample job that fills every tab with realistic data, including a fully worked Room Type, a Common Attribute, Alternates/VE, and a Window Sill Schedule. It's the best way to learn: click Load Training Project, explore freely, and Reset to wipe any changes back to the original. Your real work is parked safely and restored when you exit. While it's active, the project switcher shows only the training project — your real projects are hidden, not deleted — and nothing you do in it is written to your real project registry or shared-drive folders. Exit training to bring your real project list back.
    ⚡ Automation
    Toggle rules that push data between modules automatically — award → schedule & work orders, engineering release → production, PO changes → materials due, and optional auto-push to PostgreSQL. Every rule is individually on/off, and the editable "production start offset" sets how many days after award production begins.
    PostgreSQL
    Optional. Enter your connection details, generate the 16-table schema, and (with the companion bridge running) create the schema and push project data. Or just copy/download the SQL and run it yourself.
    File locations
    Reference paths to where each project's JSON lives on the shared drive.
    New employee? Start by loading the training project, then walk through this Help guide tab by tab with the sample data in front of you. Everything you read here is already filled in on test-project.

    Pricing tiers & the rate matrix

    ▶

    Every rate lives in three columns. The Project Tier you set in the sidebar decides which one new line items pull from:

    • Commercial — leaner rates for competitive / volume work
    • Standard — the default residential/custom column
    • Premium — high-end / architectural millwork
    Changing a rate only affects new line items. To re-price an existing line to the current matrix, click its tier button on that line. Edit the matrix itself on the ⚙ Pricing & Library tab and hit ↻ Sync All Pricing.
    Live Unit Rate Matrix — all tiers
    CategoryUnitCommercialStandardPremium

    Reflects your current saved matrix. Units: lin ft, sq ft, sq in, each, or hour depending on category.

    Proposals, addenda & RFIs

    ▶

    Delivering the proposal. On Summary: write the scope (or hit ⚡ Auto-Draft Scope to generate one from your line items), review inclusions/exclusions and the cost breakdown by area, fill terms & schedule, then Preview and Print / PDF. Clients read the scope first — get that right before fussing line items.

    Addenda & RFIs. On Addenda & RFIs, log each addendum with an acknowledgment status and route architect RFIs. Use "No Effect — Reviewed, No Impact" to close items cleanly. Optionally include the log in the proposal.

    • RFI Blast — creates Gmail drafts to a distribution list. Nothing sends automatically; you review in Gmail.
    • Letter of Transmittal — itemized cover sheet for submittals, also draft-only.
    Recipients for blasts and transmittals come from your CRM contacts and distribution lists — build those out once and reuse them.

    Saving, syncing & backups

    ▶

    The save dot next to the project name tells you the state:

    • Green — all changes saved to this browser
    • Amber — unsaved edits in flight (clears in a moment)

    Local autosave. Work is written to this browser continuously — close the tab and it's still here when you return. It's tied to this browser on this machine, so it isn't a backup on its own.

    Google Drive sync. Click Set Save Location in the header and pick a Drive folder once. After that, the project writes to maxcraft_{name}_{date}.json in that folder automatically. Your Bid Log and CRM save alongside it as their own JSON files.

    Manual moves. Export downloads the project JSON anywhere; Import loads one back in. + New starts a fresh project — export first if the current one isn't backed up.

    Before you switch machines or clear browser data: Export the project (or confirm Drive sync is set). Local autosave does not travel between computers.

    Tips & best practices

    ▶
    • Set the tier before adding lines. Rates lock in at the moment a line is created, so pick Standard/Commercial/Premium up front to avoid re-pricing later.
    • Build the Item Library. Anything you quote repeatedly — a standard base cabinet, crown, toe-kick — add it once and drop it in on every job.
    • Name elevations the way the architect does. Matching sheet/detail callouts makes RFIs and transmittals far cleaner.
    • Let Finish auto-fill. The square footage comes from your cabinet faces — add lines first, then open Finish & Paint and it pre-fills.
    • Enable only what applies. Mobilization and Prevailing Wage stay out of the total until you toggle them on.
    • Use Auto-Draft Scope as a starting point, then edit — it reads your estimate but your judgment writes the final language.
    • Log every bid. The Bid Log with lead source is how you learn which sources actually convert.
    ❓

    Troubleshooting

    ▶
    "Set Save Location" did nothing / no folder picker appeared
    The Drive folder feature uses the File System Access API, supported in Chrome and Edge on desktop. On Safari, Firefox, or mobile, use Export / Import instead — your work still autosaves locally.
    Drive stopped syncing after I reopened the app
    Browsers re-ask for folder permission on a new session. Open Set Save Location and re-grant access to the same folder.
    A rate change didn't update my existing lines
    Matrix edits apply to new lines only. Click the tier button on each existing line to re-price it, or use ↻ Sync All Pricing on the Pricing tab.
    My project vanished
    Local autosave is per-browser. A different browser, a different machine, or cleared site data won't show it. Re-import your exported JSON, or open it from your Drive folder.
    Finish square footage shows zero
    It's derived from cabinet line items — add those on the Estimate tab first, then reopen Finish & Paint.
    A change order isn't in the total
    Only approved COs roll in. Set the CO status to Approved.
    Still stuck? Export your project JSON before troubleshooting — it's a complete snapshot you can always reload.
